about.title: Fairfield Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fairfield sits where I-80 commuter traffic meets the daily flow of Travis Boulevard, North Texas Street and Air Base Parkway, and the collision record reflects that mix. In 2025, the city's final tally showed 645 injury collisions, with 912 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when workers are heading home across Solano County. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow can feel scattered: medical visits, a car you cannot drive, and an adjuster who wants to talk right away. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list. We are not a law firm. Our free service matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims against a public agency can carry a much shorter window, sometimes six months. Reaching out early helps protect your evidence and your timeline.

items.title: Deadlines Get Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California's two-year limit sounds generous until you learn that a claim involving a city vehicle or roadway condition may need to be filed within six months. The attorney you are matched with will sort out which clock applies to you.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, you can still recover even if you shared some blame for the crash; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers sometimes suggest otherwise, which is one reason to avoid giving a recorded statement before you have counsel.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and our connection service is always free.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling me after my crash on I-80 near Fairfield. Do I have to give a statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give the other party's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so early can lock you into details before you know the full extent of your injuries. Be polite, take down their contact information, and let an attorney handle the conversation. Your own policy may require cooperation, but that is a separate matter your attorney can walk you through.

items.question: What evidence should I save after a car accident in Fairfield?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the road, and any visible injuries, along with the police report number from Fairfield PD or CHP. Save medical records, repair estimates, and receipts for anything you paid out of pocket. Write down witness names while they are fresh, and hold onto the damaged vehicle or at least document it thoroughly before repairs.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in California?
items.answer: Most injury claims must be filed within two years of the crash. If a government entity is involved, such as a city bus or a defective roadway, you may have as little as six months to file a formal claim first. Because those windows are firm, it is wise to speak with an attorney well before either deadline approaches.
